sections.html:
Deeds go to the Register of Deeds at 234 W. Baraga Avenue, Marquette, MI 49855. The counter phone is (906) 225-8415, and weekday hours are 8 to 5. Documents sent through an e-recording vendor can be submitted around the clock, though staff work them between 8 and 4.

Michigan follows a race-notice rule, so the buyer who records first outranks a later claimant. Documents are processed in the order they arrive, which is why closings tend to record on funding day.

Three desks at the courthouse touch most house sales here:

  • The Register of Deeds, for the deed itself, mortgage releases and copies
  • The County Treasurer, at (906) 225-8425, for tax history and delinquent real property bills
  • Equalization and Tax Roll, at (906) 225-8405, for ownership records and parcel maps

sections.h2: Selling a home in Marquette County
sections.html:
Marquette County is large and thinly settled, with Lake Superior along its north edge. The cities are Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee, and Northern Michigan University sits in the county seat. The county had 66,017 residents in April 2020 and an estimated 68,064 by July 2025, making it the most populous county in the Upper Peninsula.

Owners value a typical house at $216,500, and 69.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Typical gross rent is $949 a month. Parcels near the range towns can have long chains of ownership, so ask your title company how far back it will search.

Twenty-two local units assess property inside the county. Assessing, bills and zoning questions start with the unit where the parcel sits, not with the Baraga Avenue offices.

  • Cities: Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee
  • Townships, A to M: Champion, Chocolay, Ely, Ewing, Forsyth, Humboldt, Ishpeming, Marquette and Michigamme
  • Townships, N to W: Negaunee, Powell, Republic, Richmond, Sands, Skandia, Tilden, Turin, Wells and West Branch

Winters are cold here, so allow for weather when you schedule a showing or an inspection.

Page count does not matter: one deed is $30.00 whether it runs two pages or twenty. The state remonumentation charge and the register's automation charge are built into that amount, so the window adds nothing else for the recording.

Charges at the Marquette County recording counter
ServiceAmount
File a deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Each extra instrument released within one paper$3.00
Treasurer's certificate attached to a warranty deed$5.00
Certified copy stamp$5.00
Ordinary copy, per sheet$1.00
Plat copy, per sheet$2.00
Clerk-run name search$0.50 a year, $5.00 minimum
Copy of a record made before 1983$7.50 tract fee added

Transfer tax is separate and applies to any taxable deed. You can pay at the counter by cash, check or card, with a processing charge on cards.

The grantor, whoever signs the property over, pays the tax. The deed must state the total consideration. If the price is kept off the deed, a valuation affidavit fills the gap, and the office files it free as long as the deed notes that one exists.

Under MCL 207.525 the state portion is $3.75 for each $500 step of the price, with any remainder counted as another step. Call the office for the county's per-step amount before you finalize a net sheet.

MCL 207.526 exempts some deeds if the grantor says so in the text. Sellers lean on these most:

  • Consideration below $100
  • A deed from an individual to a child or grandchild
  • Transfers following foreclosure, or a deed given to avoid it
  • A land contract that has not yet delivered legal title
  • A corrective quitclaim that only repairs a title flaw

sections.h2: Why a deed gets sent back
sections.html:
Usually the cause is a defect under MCL 565.201. Staff cannot prepare a deed or give legal advice, and only original signatures are recorded, which rules out faxes and photocopies. A "true copy" of a court order is also refused, since the court itself must certify it.

Defects that get a deed returned:

  • Signer names printed under the signatures that disagree with the notary block
  • No mailing address for the buyer, or no name and address for whoever prepared the deed
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue, or type under 10 point
  • Less than 2 1/2 inches of clear space at the top of page one
  • An opening line that names more than one recordable event
  • Full Social Security numbers left on the page

Anything not in English needs an English translation attached.

For warranty deeds and land contracts, the treasurer must vouch that the parcel's taxes were paid in each of the five years before the deed (MCL 211.135). Plain quitclaims escape the rule. The treasurer works from the Courthouse Annex, weekdays 8 to 5, at (906) 225-8425.

On March 1 each year the townships and cities pass their unpaid real property bills up to the county treasurer, who then collects them. Debit and credit cards are taken on those delinquent accounts. An owner who is behind can pay before asking for the certificate, or have the title company settle the balance from sale proceeds.

The office also issues tax histories, handy when a buyer wants to see past billing on a parcel.

Online, the index and images start with deeds dated January 1, 1980 and with mortgages and miscellaneous papers dated January 1, 1983. Earlier books can be read only at the office.

E-recording runs through CSC, ePN, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. Some document types cannot go this way, so title companies check with their vendor first, and any rejection is returned electronically.

Beware outside companies charging $50 or more for a certified deed copy that the county sells for as little as $1 a page. Owners may also enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert service.

sections.h2: What happens to your tax bill after closing
sections.html:
Recording the deed sets off a taxable value reset. MCL 211.27a gives the buyer 45 days to report the transfer to the local assessor, and the following year's taxable value becomes the state equalized value. The register reports recorded transfers to assessors at least once a month.

The Equalization office recommends equalized values to the Board of Commissioners, prepares about 50,000 tax statements a year and keeps ownership maps. The printed assessment roll sells for $0.15 a page with a $35 minimum.

Before closing, call (906) 225-8405 for a tax code number or parcel map, and ask the local unit what the next bill is likely to be.

sections.h2: Steps for recording your sale deed
sections.html:
A clean recording usually goes in this order. First, the title company or closing agent proofs the deed against the defect list above. Second, if it is a warranty deed, the treasurer certifies five years of paid taxes. Third, the signed original goes to the register by hand, by mail or through an e-recording vendor, with the $30.00 fee and any transfer tax. Fourth, the buyer reports the transfer to the local assessor within 45 days.

If you are selling for cash to a buyer who handles the paperwork, much of this still applies, but the buyer's closing agent carries the filing steps. Ask for a copy of the recorded deed once it is indexed.

faqs.q: How much is a flat deed filing in Marquette County?
faqs.a: It is $30.00 whatever the page count, which already covers the state survey and automation portions. Each additional instrument released in the same paper is $3.00.

faqs.q: Who has to pay the transfer tax in Marquette County?
faqs.a: The grantor, which in a sale is the seller. The state takes $3.75 for each $500 step of the price and the county adds its own amount. A deed to a child or grandchild may be exempt if it says so.

faqs.q: Can I mail a photocopy of my signed deed to the Marquette County recorder?
faqs.a: No. Only originals with live signatures are recorded, and court orders need the court's certification. Phone (906) 225-8415 first to check the paperwork.

faqs.q: Does my Marquette County warranty deed need a certificate from the treasurer?
faqs.a: Yes, and so do land contracts. The treasurer confirms the preceding five years of taxes are paid, and the fee sheet lists $5.00 for the certification. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

faqs.q: How old are the Marquette County records I can search online?
faqs.a: Deeds go back to January 1, 1980, and mortgages and miscellaneous papers to January 1, 1983. For older books, visit the office on Baraga Avenue.
